key_insight: The paper reports the first synthesis of anhydrous cubic Na$_2$IrCl$_6$ single crystals, completing the A$_2$IrCl$_6$ vacancy-ordered iridate family and revealing antiferromagnetic order at 1.91 K.
engineering_relevance: This new cubic Na-based iridate provides a structurally well-defined platform for studying spin-orbit coupling, crystal-field effects, and potential $J_{eff}=1/2$ Kitaev physics in vacancy-ordered double perovskites.
method: Structural and thermal characterization to confirm cubic phase and absence of lattice water
Magnetic measurements to identify the antiferromagnetic transition
evidence_signal: The abstract reports thermogravimetric confirmation of no lattice water, thermal stability up to 453 K, and an antiferromagnetic transition temperature of 1.91 K.
watch_item: The magnetic transition occurs only at very low temperature, so practical device relevance is indirect and the claimed $J_{eff}=1/2$ ground state remains a candidate rather than a demonstrated conclusion.
paper_title: Na$_2$Ir$^\text{IV}$Cl$_6$: The Missing Member of the Perfectly Cubic Vacancy Ordered $A_2$IrCl$_6$ Family, Another Potential $J_{eff}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$ Ground State Candidate
